author: Times Radio
description:
In the ‘lads’ culture of the Noughties, convicted rapist Russell Brand hid in plain sight. David Walliams - another performer rising to fame in that period - has been accused of sexually assaulting a 15-year-old schoolgirl and abusing his celebrity to groom teenage girls for sex. He denies the claims and has not been charged with any wrongdoing. In a statement he said ‘I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.' So how did the Noughties help shape and excuse predatory conduct? And is the fightback of women and girls finally on - are they finally being believed?

Guest: Sarah Ditum, contributor, The Times, and author of Toxic: Women, Fame and the Noughties
